findings.title: The redelivery case was green without a redelivery
findings.mechanism: The acknowledgement window is the shortest the pinned broker supports. RabbitMQ evaluates the timeout at one minute intervals and does not support values below one minute, so the delivered spec's ten seconds asserted a window that was never applied.
findings.proof: deliveries=2, firstDiscarded, effects=3 counted without deduplication, ready=0, unacked=0, and the run's own broker log carrying 'Timeout used: 60000 ms'. The assertion on probe.Faults was removed together with its collection and method: nothing ever filled it.

findings.title: The exclusivity conflict proved its own timeout
findings.mechanism: Ownership separates saying the channel is finished from taking it away. ChannelLifetime keeps the broker's own ShutdownEventArgs, invalidates immediately without blocking, hands each operation a lease for its whole duration, and disposes exactly once and only when the last lease is gone. A caller arriving afterwards receives the stored real reason. Topology operations run sequentially on the shared channel, so the first failure is the broker's own. Reply code 405 is recognised only as a real reply code — no prose, no Exception.Data as the carrier — and stays terminal, while 406 and genuine transient failures keep their retry.
findings.cause: RabbitMQ completes a refused operation's continuation with the real reply code and only then raises its shutdown notification. Disposing from inside that notification pulled the channel out from under a caller still unwinding, and the client's own finally then threw ObjectDisposedException over the broker's answer. Measured: five declares, five refusals with reply code 405, four of them replaced before anything could read them.

proof.lifetime: Six deterministic specs on TaskCompletionSource and barriers, no sleeps: immediate refusal after invalidation, no disposal while an operation runs, disposal exactly once however often it is asked, the broker's reason reaching a later caller as the same instance, nothing invented when there is no reason, and the owner's own disposal waiting for the running operation.
proof.integration: All five exclusivity specs pass. The conflict surfaces in 12.9 s against a bound budget of 20 s, where it previously took 33 to 60 s.
proof.brokerAttempts: Counted from the broker log, not from a fault counter: five resource_locked answers for five specs, so exactly one attempt each and no retry loop.

findings.title: The setup error of the test harness was swallowed
findings.mechanism: Both close sites log the original failure at error level, close best effort inside their own guard, and rethrow bare so the stack of the throw site survives.
findings.proof: Four specs and four mutations. Removing the rethrow turns three red; replacing it with 'throw ex' turns the stack spec red; leaving the close reason untrimmed changes nothing on its own, and only rethrowing the close failure as well changes the outcome — which is what proves the close really ran and really failed in the row before.

findings.title: The job service lifecycle had no owner
findings.mechanism: Stop and BusStarted run under one gate. Admission is a single decision under the same lock Stop takes, and a job admitted but not yet registered counts as outstanding for the drain. The heartbeat belongs to the generation that created it: an owned loop with cancellation and an awaitable end, so Stop returns only once its publication has finished.
findings.proof: Twelve specs and seven mutations, including two deterministic race specs that synchronise between the stopping check and the registration, and inside a blocked heartbeat publication.

crossCuttingInvariant.statement: A failure while cleaning up never replaces the failure that caused it, and a clean up failure after a delivered operation does not turn it into a reported one.
crossCuttingInvariant.proof: Five transport neutral specs in the core assembly, including the idempotency boundary named explicitly, and the mutation that puts the clean up failure back in front, which turns two of them red.
crossCuttingInvariant.note: Secondary clean up failures are recorded at error level with their operation and context rather than only at debug level.
